name: Hot-water heating boiler

combustion.note: Vented to a chimney or wall vent: check the vent and any vent damper before firing. Needs mains for its pump and controls (an oil burner alone draws up to 5.8 A at 120 V, Beckett AFG). kW is fuel input (CGa gas boiler), not heat output.

comps.spec: Circulator pump that pushes the water round the radiator or baseboard loops; mains-powered, so no pump, no heat in a power cut
comps.loc: On the supply or return pipe beside the boiler; one per zone on some systems

comps.spec: Expansion tank: takes up the water's growth as it heats (Wikipedia hydronics). Weil-McLain says a boiler gauge reading over 24 psig, or a relief valve that keeps weeping, can mean the tank isn't working (Weil-McLain user manual)
comps.loc: Hung from the pipes or ceiling near the boiler

comps.spec: Pressure relief valve with a lift lever and a metal discharge pipe run to a safe place. Never plug, cap or remove it: a closed boiler without one can burst (Wikipedia hydronics). Discharge is scalding (Weil-McLain user manual)
comps.loc: Top or side of the boiler

comps.spec: Zone valves, one per thermostat zone, opening that loop to the boiler
comps.loc: On the supply pipes near the boiler

comps.spec: Drain valve for emptying the boiler before a freeze, only on a system that holds plain water, not antifreeze (Weil-McLain user manual). Let the water cool first, and run a hose to a drain (InspectApedia boiler drain)
comps.loc: Low on the boiler and at low points of the piping

comps.spec: Gas valve with a spark-ignited pilot on gas models (Resideo VR8204 or VR8304 on the Weil-McLain CGa). Stays on the gas line
comps.loc: Burner compartment behind the front jacket panel

comps.spec: Spark igniter for the pilot (gas), or on an oil-fired boiler a solid-state igniter making 14,000 to 20,000 V peak (NORA ignition). Power off before touching the electrodes or cables
comps.loc: Burner compartment, or on top of the oil burner

comps.spec: Pilot flame sensor that proves the flame
Pressure-temperature gauge, water temperature sensor and low-water cut-off
comps.loc: On the boiler and its supply pipe

comps.spec: Water in the boiler and loops; may hold treatment chemicals or glycol antifreeze: not for drinking
Jacket panels over a cast-iron boiler (Weil-McLain CGa) or another heat exchanger: heavy

buildings.loc: Basement, in older houses and some new ones with in-floor heat

notes: It needs mains power: in a power cut the pump and controls stop, and in cold weather a power cut can mean frozen plumbing and water damage within hours (Weil-McLain user manual). If the building will freeze, the boiler and loops can be drained, but not if they hold antifreeze (Weil-McLain user manual). Turn the boiler and its gas off first, let the water cool, and never add cold water to a hot boiler: thermal shock can crack the heat exchanger (Weil-McLain user manual). Close the water feed, run a hose from the drain valve to a safe drain, and open a bleeder high up so air can replace the water (InspectApedia boiler drain). Never put automotive antifreeze in: its silicates can sludge the system (Heating Help antifreeze), and Weil-McLain says no automotive, standard or even hydronic glycol goes into its boilers, so read your own boiler's manual before adding any (Weil-McLain user manual). If it overheats or the gas won't shut off, shut the gas off at a point outside the boiler and don't switch off or unplug the pump (Weil-McLain user manual). Don't fire a boiler whose burner or controls have been sprayed or under water: Weil-McLain says it risks fire, explosion and shock and must be replaced, or fully repaired and inspected (Weil-McLain user manual). A steam boiler is different: Weil-McLain gives 15 psig as its gauge limit against 24 psig for hot water, and steam boilers have a water gauge glass and low-water cut-off to watch (Weil-McLain user manual). The draining advice here is for hot-water systems.
